channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Female artisanal miners in Kono report systemic sexual violence
item.description: Women working in abandoned diamond and gold pits in Jaiama Nimikor face persistent threats of rape and harassment while seeking a livelihood.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burners cut down fruit trees, EPA official says
item.description: Only 36% of Sierra Leoneans have access to electricity and just 15% have clean cooking, according to the government's National Energy Compact.

item.title: Civil society group demands dismissal of Sierra Leone's finance minister
item.description: A coalition calling itself the CSOs Consortium on Public Accountability says Finance Minister Sheku Ahmed Fantamadi Bangura should be removed immediately.

item.title: Sierra Leone's vice presidency has never led to the presidency
item.description: Analyst Foday M. Daboh argues the office has repeatedly failed as a route to power, and questions whether the current vice president is already too late.

item.title: Ghanaian disability advocates push for climate action inclusion
item.description: Persons with disabilities are disproportionately affected by climate change but excluded from negotiations.

item.title: Nigeria's central bank to decide on interest rates on November 23
item.description: The Monetary Policy Committee meets on November 23 and 24 to set the Monetary Policy Rate, now 23% after a cut from 26.5% in September.

item.title: Senegal's ENAMC drama students win prizes at festivals in Algiers and Rabat
item.description: The troupe took a Special Jury Prize in Rabat in October 2026 and another in Algiers in July, with one student winning the best male performance award.

item.title: Wagner group intensifies gold mining in Central African Republic
item.description: While Ndassima gold activities draw political attention, Wagner's industrial gold extraction also expands in Yidéré.

item.title: Grand Palm hosts final gin experience of 2026
item.description: Despite rain, Gaborone's gin enthusiasts gathered for premium pours, music, and social connection.

item.title: Burkinabè exiles in Ivory Coast answer military regime's charges
item.description: Former officials, soldiers and journalists living abroad are accused of apology for terrorism and incitement to rebellion, and some face extradition requests.

item.title: Salah becomes Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer in 5-0 win over Malawi
item.description: The 34-year-old forward reached 70 international goals with a Panenka penalty in stoppage time at Cairo International Stadium.

item.title: Namibia president flags engineer shortage
item.description: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah says Namibia needs more qualified technical professionals to build and run infrastructure.

item.title: Lahaiba FA beat Medina FC 4-3 on penalties to win SESDO League Cup
item.description: Lahaiba FA won the Serrekunda East Sports Development Organization (SESDO) 2026 Africell League Cup after a goalless draw, taking the penalty shootout 4-3 at the East Mini Stadium.

item.title: Djibouti urges Francophonie to reinvest in peace at Phnom Penh summit
item.description: Djibouti's foreign minister told heads of state that lasting prosperity requires justice, dialogue and solidarity, not just the absence of conflict.

item.title: Butembo civil society warns Ebola strike by care workers could hurt response
item.description: Health workers in Butembo and Katwa are striking for two months of unpaid wages, a revised pay scale and better equipment.

item.title: Benin's UP-R party sets first ordinary congress for early 2027
item.description: The party's National Council approved preparations for the congress, which will end its transitional period and update its foundational texts in Cotonou.

item.title: Togo elites accused of compromising values for power
item.description: Intellectuals and citizens once seen as moral guardians now align with President Faure Gnassingbé's government for personal gain.

item.title: MMM examines Local Government Bill implications
item.description: Village councils dissolve on November 22 as the MMM party reviews a new legal framework for local elections.

item.title: PCN denies shielding Kano drug dealers, says it sealed 1,631 outlets
item.description: The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria says it sealed 1,631 pharmaceutical premises in Kano State this year and has inspected 2,304 drug outlets.

item.title: UN economic commission urges African states to fund health data systems
item.description: Africa spends about US$145 billion a year on health, but planners often work from incomplete birth, death and population figures.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea hosts national boxing championship
item.description: Over 70 boxers from 14 clubs will compete in Malabo for the National Boxing Championship 2026.

item.title: Malawi prison officers sign mental wellness pact
item.description: A survey of 4,142 officers in the Southern Region revealed widespread distress from debt, alcohol, and family issues.

item.title: Hundreds march in Bangui against fuel price rise and high cost of living
item.description: The Bloc Républicain pour la Défense de la Constitution (BRDC) led the peaceful protest along Avenue des Martyrs on Friday morning.

item.title: Namibian universities urged to add compulsory job-search module
item.description: A proposal would require every degree and diploma programme to teach CVs, cover letters and interview skills.

item.title: Lusaka police and council detain 54 over 'Chi Cup' drinking
item.description: Police and council officers swept the area near two Lusaka colleges, catching buyers and drinkers of the illicit spirit known as 'Chi Cup'.

item.title: DR Congo minister seeks genocide recognition in London
item.description: Human rights minister Samuel Mbemba urged UK institutions to sanction Paul Kagame and recognize Congolese genocides.

item.title: Zambia proposes joint food showcase with Japan
item.description: The proposal aims to link chefs, producers, and investors to boost trade and tourism.

item.title: Ramzy-14K aims to elevate Chadian music
item.description: The N'Djaména-based artist blends Afrobeat and Amapiano to create urban music for youth.

item.title: Gambia election: Nine cleared for December 5 vote
item.description: Incumbent Adama Barrow and veteran opposition leader Ousainou Darboe are among the nine candidates cleared to stand.

item.title: Six workers dead as eight-storey building collapses near Nairobi
item.description: All 405 workers at the site have been accounted for, but the cause is still under investigation, with formwork failure suspected.

item.title: Eswatini coaches face decade-long CAF A licence gap
item.description: Eswatini has not offered the CAF A coaching licence since 2017, leaving local coaches unable to meet new continental standards.

item.title: Sugar surge lifts Eswatini manufacturing growth
item.description: Food processing rose 27 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, driven by a 53.5 per cent increase in sugar production.

item.title: Cape Verdeans vote for sixth president
item.description: Six candidates are vying for the presidency in Sunday's election, presenting diverse visions for the nation's future.

item.title: Benghazi book fair session explains Marrakesh Treaty access rules
item.description: Speakers at the fifth Benghazi International Book Fair said the treaty lets books be converted into accessible formats without prior permission from authors.

item.title: Kokari residents briefed on road safety, gender violence and HIV risks
item.description: The awareness drive is part of social measures accompanying road works on lot 6 of a World Bank and AIIB-backed rural connectivity project.

item.title: Moroccan finance committee records 20.76% absence during 2027 budget talks
item.description: Of 287 amendments proposed to the 2027 Finance Bill, the government accepted only 59 and rejected 116 after eight working days of review.

item.title: Mauritania orders EU fishing boats back to port as deal lapses
item.description: Mauritania's coast guard has told European Union fishing vessels to stop work and head to Nouadhibou before the protocol expires at midnight.

item.title: Street racers turn wet Malawi road into a racetrack
item.description: A video shows cars speeding at night on a rain-soaked dual carriageway with spectators metres from the traffic.

item.title: Morocco Week to explore trade and investment in Nouakchott
item.description: The event, from November 16 to 22, aims to boost economic ties between Mauritania and Morocco.

item.title: Odai elected NDC Greater Accra Deputy Youth Organiser
item.description: Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai won the post by a single vote over his closest rival in Saturday's regional executive elections.

item.title: Benin loses 2% of farmland in two years
item.description: Government aims to halt the decline of cultivable land, which has dropped from 43% to 41% since 2021.

item.title: Four in five Malawians with diabetes never diagnosed, campaigners say
item.description: Health groups want government to fund screening, early diagnosis and awareness, especially at primary healthcare level.

item.title: Algeria beat Togo 1-0 in CAN 2027 qualifier in Tizi Ouzou
item.description: Defender Ramy Bensebaïni headed the only goal in the 76th minute, from a cross by Hadj Moussa, as Algeria took three points in front of their own fans.

item.title: Culturama offers free diabetes screening in N'Djamena
item.description: The cultural association Culturama organized free diabetes testing at the Idriss Mahamat Ouya stadium on World Diabetes Day.

item.title: South Sudan delays elections to February 2027
item.description: The delay was blamed on ongoing political strife and flare-ups of violence, with voter registration complicated because many South Sudanese lack state-recognized identification.

item.title: Malabo French school wins national VÍA 2026 final
item.description: The winning school will now represent Equatorial Guinea in the programme's international phase, scheduled for December.

item.title: Tiassalé residents asked to give views on new Bandama bridge
item.description: A new bridge over the Bandama River will be built as part of a five-kilometre road, and the environmental study is now open to public comment.

item.title: Tunisian minister meets diaspora in Ghana
item.description: Foreign Minister Mohamed Ali Nafti discussed consular services and bilateral ties with Tunisians in Accra.

item.title: Sierra Leone seeks $1 billion AU Peace Fund
item.description: The nation also proposed a unified programme-based budget and a 0.2 percent import levy for member states.

item.title: Air Algérie fleet to reach nearly 100 aircraft as deliveries arrive
item.description: Air Algérie and its subsidiary Domestic Airlines will operate close to 100 aircraft once all ordered planes from Airbus, Boeing and ATR are delivered.

item.title: Ghanaian man stabbed to death in London
item.description: Metropolitan Police have launched a murder investigation into the death of 21-year-old Thomas Oduro.

item.title: Mali closes defense expo, plans biennial event
item.description: The Bamako International Defense and Security Exhibition (BAMEX’26) concluded with plans for future editions and intellectual property registration.

item.title: Mali army destroys terrorist vehicles and camp
item.description: Malian armed forces reported destroying a terrorist vehicle near Yenchechi and a camp southeast of Kidal on Friday, November 13, 2026.

item.title: Maladho Barry launches memoir on entrepreneurship and family in Conakry
item.description: The businessman presented "Mémoires Vivantes", published by L'Harmattan Guinée, at a ceremony attended by ministers, deputies and religious leaders.

item.title: Singapore approves Rwanda water filter project
item.description: The carbon-financed initiative will provide 1.8 million Rwandans with safe drinking water and reduce emissions.

item.title: Déby orders action on Am-Timan hotel and market
item.description: The president inspected three public buildings in Am-Timan, the capital of Salamat province, during a regional tour on Saturday.

item.title: MP Gratien Iracan warns DR Congo could lose control of Grand Inga project
item.description: The National Assembly declared admissible on Wednesday, 11 November, a draft law that will govern how the Grand Inga hydropower project is carried out.

item.title: Al Damane real estate agency opens in N'Djamena
item.description: The agency says it will handle property management, land registry paperwork and contract-based transactions for residents and investors.

item.title: Congo and Russia pledge to speed up military cooperation
item.description: The two governments agreed in Brazzaville to deepen military and technical ties, with Moscow floating on-site advisers for Congolese forces.

item.title: Diabetes affects 7% of Brazzaville residents
item.description: The Republic of Congo's Health Minister revealed the statistic during World Diabetes Day.

item.title: South Africa vaccinates over 90% of cattle herd against FMD
item.description: The vaccination rate surpasses the government's target, signaling progress in controlling the foot-and-mouth disease outbreak.

item.title: Holcim Egypt restarts cement line at Ain Sokhna after seven-year shutdown
item.description: The fifth production line at the Ain Sokhna plant is running again after an investment of more than EGP 1.3 billion, and is expected to create 560 jobs.

item.title: Djibouti military trains 91 soldiers
item.description: The army chief presided over the graduation of 91 soldiers, including 23 women, after a year of training.

item.title: Egypt builds 16 Sinai communities with 1,141 homes
item.description: The development includes 269 groundwater wells and 28 pumping units to support housing and agriculture.

item.title: Libya launches electronic system for foreign firms
item.description: The Ministry of Economy and Trade is piloting a new digital platform to streamline foreign company branch registrations.

item.title: Eswatini hold Malta 1-1 in first match on European soil
item.description: Captain Philani Mkhontfo scored Eswatini's first-ever goal in Europe in first-half stoppage time, even after Gift Gamedze was sent off in the 29th minute.

item.title: Senegal insurance union threatens strike over 14th month pay
item.description: Workers demand an extra month's salary as negotiations for a new collective agreement stall.

item.title: Ivory Coast, France, Gabon armies end joint security drill
item.description: Operation Fangha 2026 tested interoperability and regional threat response in Yamoussoukro.

item.title: Mali joins UEMOA farm program for 2026-2030
item.description: Ministers approved regional plans for cotton, fertilizer, and rice, aiming for 90% rice self-sufficiency.

item.title: Chad officials urge herders to respect farming calendar
item.description: Loug-Chari authorities conduct field missions to prevent farmer-herder conflicts by promoting dialogue and awareness.

item.title: Guinea and Djibouti sign carbon cooperation accord at COP31
item.description: The two environment ministers will share expertise on sovereign carbon initiatives and the development of carbon markets.

item.title: Senegal, Switzerland discuss stronger partnerships
item.description: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye met Swiss Vice-President Ignazio Cassis in Phnom Penh to explore cooperation in vocational training, health, economy, and water management.

item.title: African court rejects Ajavon relatives' damages claim against Benin
item.description: The court said the four family members never tried the domestic remedies open to them in Benin before bringing their complaint.

item.title: Togo president attends Francophonie summit in Cambodia
item.description: Faure Gnassingbé joins world leaders in Phnom Penh to discuss peace, stability, and shared prosperity.

item.title: Women from Zinder's Quranic schools hold prayer sessions for peace
item.description: Hundreds of women gathered at Zinder's André Salifou University in a reading of the Quran, held at the request of the First Lady.

item.title: Mauritania reaffirms Francophonie commitment
item.description: Foreign Minister Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug attended the 48th ministerial conference in Phnom Penh.

item.title: Hakimi stars as Morocco beats Niger 5-1 in AFCON qualifiers
item.description: Spanish daily AS names Achraf Hakimi the world's best fullback after his two goals and assist in the victory.

item.title: France welcomes UN sanctions listing of Kabila's FRN movement
item.description: Paris reaffirms its support for DR Congo's sovereignty and territorial integrity in the east.

item.title: Catholic Bishops demand school abuse investigations
item.description: Ghana's Catholic Bishops' Conference is heartbroken by allegations of sexual abuse of minors in schools and calls for immediate investigations.

item.title: Nouakchott region shares climate action at COP31
item.description: The region presented its strategy for tackling floods, coastal erosion, and water scarcity at the Antalya conference.

item.title: Niger's APME-DIRGA presents pastoralist support project in Niamey
item.description: The association gathered state services, development partners, customary authorities and herders to review the draft plan before it is finalised.

item.title: Guinea launches Simandou Mining Summit
item.description: The summit showcased infrastructure projects worth billions to diversify Guinea's economy.

item.title: Mauritius promotes higher education in Madagascar
item.description: 17 Mauritian institutions showcased study opportunities in Antananarivo.

item.title: Niger's mobilisation chief asks soldiers' wives to review national defence plan
item.description: General Mamane Souley, head of the General Mobilisation Commission, presented the plan to the wives of Niger's Defence and Security Forces in Niamey on Saturday.

item.title: JB Mpiana returns to Paris's Accor Arena for 40-year career concert
item.description: Congolese music star Jean Bedel Mpiana Tshituka was scheduled to perform at the Accor Arena in Paris on Saturday, 14 November, marking 40 years in music.

item.title: Nigeria secures $3m deal for 1,000 tomato greenhouses
item.description: The agreement, signed at COP31 in Türkiye, is meant to bring private money into climate-smart tomato farming in Kano State.

item.title: Mulbah Morlu rejoins Liberia's CDC party
item.description: The former national chairman says he is returning as an ordinary member and is not seeking leadership.

item.title: Nigeria warns citizens about travel via Addis Ababa airport
item.description: Abuja advises travellers with health conditions to be cautious due to the airport's high altitude.

item.title: IFAD, AFD sign deal for rural transformation in Nigeria
item.description: The co-financing agreement backs the Value Chain Programme in Northern Nigeria, which is designed to cut poverty and improve nutrition in rural areas.

item.title: Kenya holds fuel pump prices with Sh4.6bn subsidy
item.description: The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority says pump prices will not change for 30 days even though the cost of all three fuels rose between September and October.

item.title: Morocco learns its beach soccer schedule for the CAN in Senegal
item.description: The Confederation of African Football released the official calendar for the 2026 beach soccer Cup of Nations, which runs from November 28 to December 6 in Saly, Senegal.

item.title: Malawi protest group suspends fuel and blackout demonstrations for talks
item.description: The Concerned Citizens of Malawi-People Power Movement had planned nationwide protests on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, over fuel shortages and electricity blackouts.

item.title: Senegal minister open to new legal expert status
item.description: Justice Minister Moussa Sarr considers a new professional path for law graduates struggling to enter traditional legal careers.

item.title: Zerhouni appointed head of Algerian diaspora scientific council
item.description: President Tebboune names the Algerian-American professor to lead the newly created body aimed at leveraging expatriate expertise for national development.

item.title: Chapo seeks UAE investment during Abu Dhabi visit
item.description: President Daniel Chapo is in the United Arab Emirates on a three-day working visit from 13 to 15 November to strengthen ties and draw new investment.

item.title: Morocco sends Head of Government to 20th Francophonie Summit
item.description: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri arrived in Phnom Penh on Saturday to represent King Mohammed VI at the two-day summit.

item.title: Mother transfers daughter to private clinic after public hospital delays
item.description: A mother alleges her minor daughter did not receive specialist care and was transferred without her knowledge from a public hospital.

item.title: Museveni pledges tax exemption for doctors' salaries
item.description: President Museveni also promised Shs125 billion for a doctors' Sacco and urged a shift to preventive healthcare.

item.title: Malabo police seize 28,250mg of tramadol from Cameroon ship
item.description: Two Cameroonian crew members of the vessel Queen Rebeca were arrested as they allegedly prepared to hand over the painkiller for sale.

item.title: South Sudan begins voter registration amid logistical strain
item.description: The National Elections Commission must deliver materials to remote areas within a two-week window before the February 11, 2027 vote.
